scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Decide what the helper is for
scenes.caption: Asha frames a fictional library-enquiry helper. It suggests whether a request needs staff review; it never approves renewals or makes binding decisions. The team must define users, a comparator and acceptable errors before inspecting prepared scores.
scenes.dialogue: What decision will a prediction support?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A useful comparator
scenes.caption: The supplied pack has one hundred requests: five need staff review and ninety five are routine. An always-routine non-AI baseline looks accurate but misses every staff-review case. The team needs more than a headline percentage.
scenes.dialogue: Compare on the same cases and the same task.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Commit the acceptance plan
scenes.caption: In this exercise, a missed staff-review case costs five invented units and an unnecessary review costs one. Staff can review at most ten flagged requests per hundred. The proposed minimum recall is eighty percent. These are classroom constraints, not universal targets.
scenes.dialogue: Write the goal before reading results.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose a defensible plan
scenes.caption: Should the team choose whichever metric looks best after testing, compare different packs, or fix the task, baseline, costs and review capacity before inspecting the prepared results?
scenes.dialogue: A result should answer the question you set.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A bounded brief
scenes.caption: Asha commits the library-staff use, always-routine comparator, error costs, recall target and review capacity. An uncertain request still has a staff route. The plan can now reveal whether a candidate meets the stated purpose.
scenes.dialogue: A polished answer is not an acceptance criterion.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the evaluation lab
scenes.caption: Build the brief, commit the acceptance plan before revealing the sheet and explain when a non-AI comparator is preferable. No real library record or live model is used.
scenes.dialogue: Start with the decision and its consequences.
